status: Development draft. Written by the author of check.mjs, who also wrote the expected outcomes; agreement between the two is not independent evidence. Every case is synthetic and names a reserved .example host. No host sent any of it.
how_to_read: Each case starts from a fresh copy of the base file and applies its edits in order. The outcomes expected for the case are base_outcomes with the case's own outcomes laid over them; result is the result word.

path and from are JSON Pointers (RFC 6901) into the fixture. set puts value at path, replacing what is there; when the parent is a list, the last token is an index to replace or - to append. remove deletes the member or list entry at path. copy puts a copy of the value at from at path, placed as set places it.
targets names the one check a case is about. Where result is check_failed and targets is given, that check is the only one that fails.

issues lists the issue codes check.mjs reports for the case, each once. They are this checker's own words and are not part of the exit gate; the result word and the twenty outcomes are. A result holds at most 256 issues; when more arise, at least one is kept for every check that fails or is unknown.

exercised, where given, states counts expected in the result's exercised for that case; a count it leaves out is not stated. body_stays_schema_valid names a body that still matches its schema after the edits.

built cases are not written as edits: some are not JSON, and the others would be very long. Each gives a recipe. Where a recipe starts from the base file, the input is that fixture written as JSON in any way that stays within the size limit.

tripwire.note: What I.NO_CREDENTIAL looks for, with regular expressions in ECMAScript syntax and their flags. Adapted from work/0.1/check.mjs. A match is a failure whatever the value is; no match establishes nothing.
tripwire.secret_shapes_read: Every field name in the fixture, and every string value except the four places under not_read.
address_rules: A string value is in an address field when the nearest field name above it is one of address_fields: it is that field's value, or an entry of a list that is. Such a value that matches address_start is one address, taken whole. In every other string value that is read, each run that matches address_run is an address.
An address in an address field fails when it does not parse as a URL by the WHATWG URL Standard (href_unparseable). An address inside other text is not asked to parse.
An address fails when the text between :// and the next /, ? or # holds @ (href_userinfo).

An address fails when its query or its fragment holds a pair whose key is credential-named and whose value is not empty (href_credential_query_key, href_credential_fragment_key). The query is the text after the first ? and before the first #; the fragment is the text after the first #. Each is read as application/x-www-form-urlencoded pairs: split at &, each pair split at its first =, then + and percent-escapes decoded.

credential_named.normalise: Put a break between a lower-case letter or a digit and an upper-case letter that follows it. Lower-case the key. Split it at every run of characters other than a to z and 0 to 9, drop empty parts, and join the parts with _.
credential_named.note: Applied to the normalised key. The name alone decides: token=USDC fails. key, auth, sig and pass count only as the whole key. code and state are not listed, and a token part straight after a page part is a paging key.
